NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using gas-side $\Delta P$ thresholding or basket weight sensors to detect plugging. Your mechanism departs by using a physics-based "Thermal Conductance Efficiency Index" derived from existing gas and air temperatures, which decouples the specific heat capacity drop of the flue gas due to dust/fly ash accumulation from the geometric flow area restriction, providing a leading indicator of fouling density before $\Delta P$ spikes. The failure-physics connection is that fouling adds a thermal resistance layer on the gas side, reducing the heat transfer coefficient ($h_g$) and consequently the gas-side temperature drop, which is detectable in the existing temperature data.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is the gas-side heat transfer coefficient degradation due to fouling resistance ($R_f$). The standard heat balance is $Q = U A \Delta T_{lm}$. Fouling increases total resistance $R_{total} = 1/h_g + R_f + ...$. As $R_f$ increases, the actual gas-side temperature drop $\Delta T_g = T_{in,g} - T_{out,g}$ decreases for a constant heat duty $Q$ (which is maintained by the boiler load). The magnitude verification: A typical Ljungstrom APH has a gas-side $\Delta T_g$ of 150-200 K. Fouling of $0.0002 \ m^2K/W$ reduces the gas-side film coefficient from ~50 W/m²K to ~45 W/m²K, a 10% drop in heat transfer effectiveness. This manifests as a measurable increase in $T_{out,g}$ (or decrease in $\Delta T_g$) of approximately 5-10 K relative to clean baseline at constant load, which is well above sensor noise.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
(a) (b) (c) Use existing DCS/SCADA historical database to extract gas inlet temperature ($T_{in,g}$), gas outlet temperature ($T_{out,g}$), gas-side differential pressure ($\Delta P_g$), and rotor drive motor current ($I_m$). (a) (b) (c) Compute the "Thermal Conductance Efficiency Index" ($E_t$) using the formula $E_t = \frac{\Delta P_g / I_m}{T_{in,g} - T_{out,g}}$, which normalizes the flow restriction proxy by the thermal performance decay. (a) (b) (c) Establish a clean-baseline reference for $E_t$ by identifying the minimum $E_t$ value recorded during the last three months of operation where the boiler was running at >90% load, tagging this as DERIVED from ALREADY-RECORDED DCS data. (a) (b) (c) Set the plugging alarm threshold at $E_t$ dropping by 15% from the clean-baseline reference, labeling this threshold as CALCULATED from the physics check (fouling resistance impact). (a) (b) (c) Integrate the $E_t$ value into the existing operator HMI screen as a new trend variable, tagged as (a) Firmware/Code update to the existing DCS logic, requiring no new hardware procurement.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: ZERO, as all inputs are ALREADY-RECORDED in the DCS; only a software logic block addition is required. Operability: The operator monitors one new trend variable ($E_t$) instead of multiple disparate readings; the burden is lower than interpreting raw $\Delta P$ which can be confused by load changes. Maintenance: No physical maintenance burden for the predictor itself, as it relies on existing calibrated sensors; if a temperature sensor fails, the predictor stops, which is the same failure mode as standard $\Delta P$ monitoring. Rough Cost Class: SAME as standard practice (software development hours only, no new instruments). The approach is lighter in operational cognitive burden because it collapses four signals into one physics-based index.
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Retrieve 6 months of ALREADY-RECORDED DCS data for $T_{in,g}$, $T_{out,g}$, $\Delta P_g$, and $I_m$. Identify two periods: Period 1 (Clean) where the APH was just cleaned and load was steady at 100%; Period 2 (Fouled) where the next basket cleaning was required after ~3 months of continuous operation. Calculate $E_t$ for both periods. Pass Criterion: The average $E_t$ in Period 2 must be >15% lower than Period 1. Kill Criterion: If the difference in $E_t$ between Clean and Fouled states is <5% (within noise), the mechanism fails to detect fouling via thermal conductance decay, and the test is falsified, requiring reversion to pure $\Delta P$ thresholding. Duration: 1 hour of data analysis.

CONSTRAINT BIND (predictor)
The primary stated indicator is gas-side differential pressure ($\Delta P_g$). The predictor uses $T_{in,g}$ and $T_{out,g}$ as the mechanism core, but explicitly includes $\Delta P_g$ in the $E_t$ numerator to maintain the primary indicator's relevance. The secondary indicator (motor current $I_m$) is used only to normalize the $\Delta P_g$ against rotor speed/load, ensuring the $\Delta P_g$ is not misinterpreted during low-load operation. The answer explicitly states that the gas temperature pair provides the *fouling physics* signal while $\Delta P_g$ provides the *flow area* signal, both necessary for the $E_t$ index, thus respecting the constraint that no new instrumentation is used.
